title: Completed internal-Hom scalar transpose on perfect point models
statement:
Fix $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and finite coefficient extensions $E\subset L\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$, $B'=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,s}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $P$ be a bounded complex of finite-projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], $P_L=P\otimes_R S$, and $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$. Constant module sheaves are denoted by underlines [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Set $K=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline P$, $H=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{P^\vee}$, $K_L=B'\otimes_{\underline S}\underline{P_L}$, and $J_L=B'\otimes_{\underline S}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P_L,S[0])}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-hom-complex]. Assume $K,H\in D^b_c(s,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Use their ordinary finite-projective internal-Hom identifications and the specified completed evaluation of [lem-pod-point-completed-evaluation]. These models and their evaluation tensor products lie in the derived-complete bounded constructible categories and have finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], uniformly over all finite reductions.
Put $F=-\otimes_B^L B'$ and let $\chi:F\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}$ be the canonical strict-cone completion map [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], where $T_{L/E}$ is [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Fix the quotient-normalized comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]: its tensor map at every finite quotient sends $(x\otimes\bar a)\otimes(y\otimes\bar b)$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes\bar a\bar b$, compatibly with the quotient transitions, and its internal-Hom arrow $\delta:T_{L/E}H\to R\mathcal Hom_{B'}(T_{L/E}K,B')$ is the transpose of the extended completed evaluation.
Under $FK\cong K_L$, given by $(b\otimes x)\otimes b'\mapsto bb'\otimes(x\otimes1)$ with inverse $b'\otimes(x\otimes a)\mapsto(1\otimes x)\otimes ab'$, and the analogous Hom-model identifications, the conjugate of $\delta$ by $\chi$ is the actual cochain map
$$\gamma:FH\longrightarrow J_L,\qquad \gamma(h\otimes a)(z\otimes b)=h(z)ab.$$
Here $h$ is a local homogeneous $B$-linear functional on $K$, $z$ a local homogeneous section of $K$, and $a,b$ local sections of $B'$, with the scalar images understood. Its uncurried evaluation is $(-1)^{\deg z\deg h}h(z)ab$. The compatibility with $\chi$ is equality of the maps from the ordinary models to the strict quotient towers, including the quotient-map product components and zero shifted-product components of the completion maps, and hence equality in $D(B')$. The maps are natural on all derived morphisms of perfect models. For $L=E$ they are the identity under multiplication and completeness. For $E\subset L\subset M$ they respect the specified integral associator obtained by conjugating the ordinary tensor associator by $\chi$; at every quotient the two successive coefficient multiplications and direct multiplication are the same. No assertion about taking sections is included.

proof.text: The displayed map FK to K_L and its displayed inverse are balanced: moving r in R or a in S across a tensor has exactly the same effect as multiplying its image in B'. Their composites send (b tensor x) tensor b' to (1 tensor x) tensor bb'=(b tensor x) tensor b' and send b' tensor (x tensor a) to ab' tensor (x tensor 1)=b' tensor (x tensor a). They preserve differentials because all coefficient scalars have degree zero. The same balancing identifies FH with the extension of the dual model. These constructions commute with restrictions, so sheafification of the presheaf tensors gives the claimed sheaf-complex identifications. Use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Stage-3 partial implementation: the ordinary transport of the two scalar implementations is the inverse of the already proved ordinaryScalarModelIso in IntegralScalarExtensionConstructible, extended termwise. Its generator equation follows by applying the inverse to ordinaryScalarModelIso_transport and cancelling the isomorphism. For uniqueness, compare the hom components degree by degree using completedScalar_tensor_ext. This proves ordinaryTransport_existsUnique without changing either ordinary scalar construction; The coefficient identification coefficientBaseChange_existsUnique is obtained by transporting the proved scalar-extension unit isomorphism of [lem-pd-sheaf-scalar-extension-constraint-coherence] through the ordinary tensor witness and then Mathlib singleMapHomologicalComplex. Its multiplication formula follows from unitForward_tmul, functoriality on tensor generators and the degree-zero single-complex comparison. Tensor-presentation extensionality and to_single_hom_ext prove uniqueness. modelBaseChange_existsUnique remains open.

proof.text: Apply lem-pod-scalar-hom-cochain-pairing to h,h_L and the chosen modelBaseChange k. Its hypotheses are exactly the two given Hom normalizations and modelBaseChange_existsUnique.choose_spec. It gives an actual cochain map gamma, together with gamma(a tensor f)(k(b tensor z))=image(h(f)(z))*a*b for every pair of degrees summing to zero and every local section. Its conclusion does not already include any derived comparison, signed uncurrying or completion square; those are supplied in the next three steps.

source.place: Second sentence: '$R\mathcal Hom$ at the point being computed over the coefficient ring'; finite-projective scalar/evaluation calculation. Completed-model part of returned steps 1, 3, 5 and 6.

proof.text: Construct signed uncurrying using the existing totalTensor functor map on gamma followed by h_L (definitionally mapBifunctorMap(identity,gamma followed by h_L)), followed by the proved evaluation chain map of lem-pod-point-sheaf-hom-maps. Fix the countable-totalization and tensor zero-preservation instances explicitly. The summand inclusion identity for mapBifunctorMap and moduleTmul_map from lem-pur-module-tensor-generator-calculus send totalElement(z,f) to totalElement(z,(gamma followed by h_L)(f)). The evaluation formula is therefore (-1)^(p*j) times the value supplied by the ordinary chain formula. Applying the coefficient single-complex identification preserves this integer scalar multiplication.

Write A'_m=(S/varpi_L^m)_s and let q_m:B' to A'_m be the quotient. Reduce e' and the ordinary scalar-association map on the representatives of step 1. The two uncurried routes at m, with the quotient-normalized tensor comparison stipulated in the item, both send (z tensor bar b) tensor (h tensor bar a) to (-1)^(pj) q_m(h(z)) bar a bar b. Quotient transitions commute with this formula since they are ring maps. The completed tensor operation is the strict limit of these reduction tensors by [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The completion augmentations of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] have the family of quotient maps as product component and zero shifted-product component. A strict tower map acts diagonally on the two products by [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. In the coordinates F(X)^(r+1)=P(X)^r direct-sum P(X)^(r+1) fixed by [def-weil-strict-roos-model], both composites in source degree r+1 are exactly (0,(q_m e')_m): applying the diagonal tower map to (0,(q_m)_m) gives this pair, as does augmenting after e'. This proves equality of actual maps into the specified shifted cones, not an inference that equality after reduction detects arbitrary derived maps. The identical computation over B, with L=E, identifies the ordinary evaluation e with the specified completed evaluation under the identity completion comparisons. For completion_implementation_transport, use the existing normalization proof of integralScalarCompletionChain_existsUnique to identify the selected chain map with the termwise ordinaryScalarModelIso followed by completedScalarChainComparison. Identify ordinaryTransport with the inverse of that same termwise isomorphism using its tensor-normalized uniqueness. Cancellation gives the strict chain equality. The cochain scalar model supplies a natural counit and its universal left-derived property; cache its actual counit in a private definition and use its proved component normalization. Universal uniqueness of left-derived functors transports the ordinary scalar functor along ordinaryTransport. The other derived implementation transport is the identity on the definitionally identical completed scalar functor. The scalarCompletion and completedScalarComparison representative equations, together with the strict chain equality, give the comparison square on good complexes. Localization extends the equality and proves uniqueness of both transports. This proves completion_implementation_transport without changing any public definition or signature. H3 proves CompletionSquare for every cochain map f: naturality supplies the square; witnessTensor_naturality moves f across an ordinary tensor generator, so the completion normalization supplies the quotient coordinate; associativity and the zero shifted-coordinate normalization supply the last coordinate. Apply this separately to gamma and to the constructed signed evaluation.

proof.text: The operation comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] is natural on the derived categories, and chi is natural there by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. The balancing isomorphisms of step 2 are the canonical tensor identifications, and the Hom-model identifications are the canonical ordinary-to-derived Hom maps stipulated in the hypotheses. They commute with tensor morphisms and precomposition. Thus conjugating the naturality square of delta by these identifications proves naturality of gamma for every derived morphism of perfect models. In particular this argument includes inverse quasi-isomorphisms; it does not require that all sheaf-derived morphisms be represented by cochain maps between the fixed models. For a cochain map u the square reads gamma_P(u^vee h tensor a)(z tensor b)=h(u(z))ab=(u_L^vee gamma_Q(h tensor a))(z tensor b). The formal derived_coherence naturality clause is exactly scalarHomOrdinary_naturality specialized to M=model(P), M'=model(Q), N=N'=B[0], a=v and b=identity. Rewrite the image of the identity by the ordinary derived scalar functor as identity. This includes arbitrary derived v.

proof.text: For L=E, multiply away the scalar factors. The formula becomes h tensor a mapped to the functional z mapped to h(z)a, which is exactly the functional ah corresponding to h tensor a. Hence gamma is the identity under multiplication. The identity case of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies chi with the specified completeness map; the coordinate equality of step 5 gives the same identity for the completed comparison. Formally, the identity conjunct of derived_coherence is the Hom conjunct (.2.2) of scalarOperationsOrdinary_unit, with the scheme map chosen to be the identity on Spec(k).

proof.text: For E contained in L contained in M put B''=widehat O_(M,s). Evaluate the two successive scalar maps on ((h tensor a) tensor c) and ((z tensor b) tensor d), with a,b in B' and c,d in B''. The result is h(z) i(a)i(b)cd, where i:B' to B''. Applying the ordinary balanced associators first gives h tensor i(a)c and z tensor i(b)d, whose direct gamma value is the same product. The signed uncurrying on either route multiplies by the same (-1)^(pj). At each M-quotient reduction these products are still equal and commute with transition ring maps. Both maps to the strict cone have these equal quotient product components and zero shifted-product components: the completion augmentations of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] are strict augmentations and strict tower maps act diagonally on both products by [def-weil-strict-roos-model], as in step 5. Finally the specified integral associator is, by the stipulated hypothesis, obtained by conjugating this ordinary associator with chi. Substitute that definition: each adjacent chi inverse followed by chi cancels, chi being invertible on these derived-complete objects by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], leaving exactly the ordinary equality just checked. This proves the required integral tower equation and its quotient-coordinate normalization. Formally, the tower conjunct of derived_coherence is the Hom conjunct (.2.2) of scalarOperationsOrdinary_tower, evaluated at the two displayed derived model objects and at the identity scheme map.
